outcome: Length of stay for women and infants
cohort: 1,722,840 women with singleton, non-anomalous births in California from 2007 to 2011, excluding those with preexisting diabetes mellitus and chronic hypertension
finding: Hospitalization costs for both mothers and infants significantly differed across pre-pregnancy BMI categories, with underweight and normal weight women having the lowest costs and the most obese category (BMI ≥50) having the highest costs.
mod_finding: Costs remained significantly different across BMI categories even after stratifying by mode of delivery and gestational age at delivery.
